question.text: Which of the following is a right of a mutual fund investor?

answer.text: Right to appoint the fund manager
Right to receive redemption proceeds within stipulated time and to file complaints with the AMC and SEBI
Right to decide which securities the fund should buy

explanation.text: The Logic: Investors are entitled to receive their redemption proceeds, access grievance redressal, and escalate complaints to SEBI through SCORES. The workbook also recognises investors' right to make nominations as per the prescribed framework. The Trap: Investors do not have a right to guaranteed returns (mutual funds are market-linked), nor do they decide on fund manager appointments or individual security selection. Those responsibilities sit with the AMC and the fund manager. Note: Investors may appoint nominees as permitted under the source's nomination framework; the specific maximum count and operational timelines should be confirmed with the latest scheme documents.
